newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom to raise ad spending.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom to raise ad spending.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc on Friday said it expects to increase its advertising budget in its 1997/98 financial year, following a sharp increase this year.

"We have substantially increased our advertising spend, and probably will next year," Robert Dunnett, a BT spokesman, told Reuters in a phone interview. "Simply put, it's been very effective," he added.

BT will spend about 100 million pounds ($166.3 million) on advertising in the current financial year, which ends March 30, 1997. The company spent about 60 million pounds on advertising in the prior year, Dunnett said. He said it is premature to estimate the advertising budget for the 1997/98 financial year, but said it is expected to rise.
The increased spending, which includes all media advertising but excludes direct marketing, reflects the hotly competitive residential phone market in Britain.

BT's "It's Good to Talk" television advertising campaign, featuring actor Bob Hoskins, has been one of its key weapons in its fight to maintain its market. Dunnett said the ad's effectiveness is reflected in an increase in the average amount of time residential customers spend on the phone -- up 77 seconds to just over 10 minutes a day over the last 18 months -- along with a steady number of customers.

BT, which until 1992 had had a duopoly with Mercury Communications, now faces competition from a host of other telephone operators, including the cable television companies. Britain's largest cable operators are majority-owned by U.S. telecommunications companies.
"The cable companies claim to be gaining 50,000 customers a month. We are not losing them." Dunnett said. "In this business standing still is equivalent to growth."

"The UK is probably the most competitive (phone) market in the world," he added. "One way or another there are about 150 competitors to BT," although he noted that many of those rivals are small companies offering niche services, such as low-priced international calling.

The "It's Good to Talk" advert with Bob Hoskins, which earlier this week won the annual advertising effectiveness award from Britain's Institute of Practitioners in Advertising, is scheduled to be retired at the end of next month. The ad featuring Hoskins has been broadcast since 1993.
"Three years as a face for BT is probably enough for him and enough for us," Dunnett said. "You won't be seeing Bob Hoskins after Christmas."

BT will continue to use the "It's Good to Talk" theme in its television adverts in 1997, but with a team of actors appearing in various ads. "They will be people who will make the right impact," Dunnett said.
